docs.text: Education is a public good FreeCampus began with a simple conviction: access to excellent learning materials should not depend on where you live, what you earn, or whether you belong to an institution. We bring together learners, educators, subject experts, editors, designers, and developers to create thoughtful materials across disciplines. The work is open, so every lesson can be examined, discussed, adapted, translated, and made better. Our principles 01 Open by default Materials should be available without fees, artificial scarcity, or hidden conditions. 02 Rigorous and humane We value accuracy and depth, expressed with clarity and respect for the learner. 03 Built together Many perspectives make stronger resources. Constructive review is part of authorship. 04 Always improving An open course is never finished. It evolves as knowledge and its community grow. A campus without gates Educators and practitioners can help shape our courses through the Instructor Network , contributing lessons, practical activities, and thoughtful review. There are no admissions forms here. No prescribed pace. You are welcome whether you are meeting a subject for the first time, returning after years away, or helping someone else understand it more deeply. Explore the subjects →

docs.text: Help build the campus You do not need to be a professor—or even an expert—to make FreeCampus better. Clear feedback from a first-time learner can be as valuable as a new chapter from an experienced teacher. Write Explain an idea Create lessons, examples, exercises, or a complete learning path in a subject you know well. Review Make it stronger Check material for accuracy, clarity, accessibility, and the questions a learner may still have. Build Improve the platform Help with the site, learning tools, documentation, testing, or other open infrastructure. Learn Share your experience Try a lesson, note where you hesitated, and help us see the material through fresh eyes. How to begin Interested in creating or reviewing a course? Explore the Instructor Network to learn how educators and practitioners can collaborate with FreeCampus. Visit the FreeCampus organization on GitHub . Look through the open projects and choose an issue that matches your interests. Introduce yourself, ask questions, and make a small first contribution. Every contribution is reviewed collaboratively. We care about the quality of the work and the experience of the people creating it. Visit FreeCampus on GitHub ↗

docs.text: Teach beyond the classroom The FreeCampus Instructor Network brings together educators and practitioners who want to help create rigorous, freely accessible learning materials. Whether you teach in a classroom, mentor a team, or explain ideas through open projects, your experience can help more people learn. Affiliated instructors collaborate with the community on lessons, exercises, and course review. Start with a subject you know well and a contribution you can sustain. Start a conversation → Ways to contribute Create Build a learning path Turn your subject knowledge into clear lessons, worked examples, and a sequence learners can follow. Practice Make ideas tangible Design purposeful exercises, quizzes, and projects that connect explanations to practical understanding. Review Strengthen a course Check accuracy, prerequisites, and learning progression. Help authors make difficult ideas easier to grasp. Adapt Reach more learners Improve accessibility, translate explanations, and bring examples from different communities and contexts. How we work together Begin with a lesson, a review, or a course proposal. Agree on the scope with the project maintainers, then develop the material openly so others can offer feedback and help improve it. Put learners first. State the prerequisites and learning goals, explain ideas clearly, and include meaningful practice. Work in the open. Use the relevant project's contribution guidance and license, and credit the people and sources behind the material. Welcome review. Discuss feedback constructively and check examples and exercises before sharing them. Choose a sustainable scope. Talk with maintainers about the time you can give and how the material will be maintained. Meet the instructors Instructor profiles will be published here as affiliations and profile details are confirmed. Each profile will connect an instructor's expertise with the courses or materials they help create, so learners can explore their work. Already contributing to a FreeCampus course? Share a short biography, your subject areas, links to your contributions, and any public profile links you would like included when you contact the maintainers. Get involved Browse our subjects and choose an existing course or a topic you would like to propose. Visit the relevant project through the FreeCampus GitHub organization . Open an issue to introduce your proposal; for a new course or a general inquiry, use the website repository . Describe your teaching or practical experience, the learners you want to support, and the contribution you have in mind. Discuss the next step with the maintainers before starting a larger course. You can contribute a small improvement at any time. Visit our contribution guide for other ways to help. Introduce your teaching idea ↗

Learn at your own pace, return whenever you need, and share what you discover. Community authors wanted Humanities · In development History & society Read sources critically, examine systems, and discover how the past continues to shape our lives. Each module combines a focused explanation, worked examples, exercises, and references for going deeper. Everything is published openly so it can be read, reused, translated, and improved.
